body:
P2-12 PLAN 3/6: IDENTITY, the N-14 fix (facts read in the code, 14 Nov 2026)
The phone has FOUR rules for "which catalogue artist is this artist": (a) libraryArtistCatalogueProvider (catalogue_providers.dart:156): same folded name and albumCount > 0, then the releases of the three best known against the library's album titles, else most fans; (b) AlertsService (alerts_service.dart:320 to 358): the FIRST same-name artist in the catalogue's own order, remembered per library artist in the phone's key-value store (alerts.catalogueArtistIds), no album-count test, so it can disagree with the page; (c) catalogueSearchProvider (request_providers.dart:243): most fans of the same-named artists; (d) openArtistByName (open_artist.dart:45): rankNamesakes, exact name then fans. The one that costs time is (a): 2 to 3 catalogue calls in a row on every visit (N-14).
The server has the pieces: artist_finder.pick_artist_picture proves an artist from ONE of its own songs (ADR-R46) and returns ArtistPicture.source_id, the catalogue's artist id, which deezer_artist_picture throws away. The phone's artist row id is the music server's artist id (its artist rows come from getArtists, sync_engine.dart:509) and artist_picture is keyed by the same id: the key both sides already have. A name key would need P2-25's normaliser (today it folds every Arabic artist to "", B-37).
DECISION: extend N-15's table; no second table, no second rule (docs/30 question 4). Migration 0014 rebuilds artist_picture as artist_catalogue (create, copy, drop, rename: SQLite cannot relax a CHECK): same key, same name, picture columns kept (outcome nullable: NULL = a visit learned the identity and nobody looked for a picture), new columns catalogue_id (NULL = the catalogue has no such artist), basis, decided_at, recheck_at, evidence (JSON: candidates, fans, the matching song or albums). One function identify_artist() beside pick_artist_picture (which it reuses) is called by the artist finder (so a picture found by song evidence records the identity at no extra request) and by the route. It lives in encore.db: backup and restore carry it.
THE RULE (one, for the whole server, ordered by cost): (1) one request, the artists named like it: exactly one same folded name with albumCount > 0 -> 'only'. (2) several -> song evidence: the track search for up to 3 of the artist's own songs; a hit counts when its title is the song's and its artist is the library artist or leads the credit -> 'song'. (3) none proves it -> the releases of the 3 best known against the library's album titles for the artist (song_ref.album) -> 'overlap' when at least one title is shared. (4) else most fans -> 'fans'. No same-name artist at all: song evidence for up to 2 songs, else a miss (catalogue_id NULL, recheck in 7 days). A catalogue that could not be asked writes nothing (B-124). Rechecks: 'fans' after 30 days or when the library's albums for the artist change; 'only', 'overlap', 'song' after 180 days; 'host' never (reserved for a Host's own choice; no screen sets it).
Two catalogue artists of one name: the library artist links to ONE; the other stays a separate unowned row in search, as today. Weakness: 'fans' can pick the wrong namesake when nothing else proves it; it is the shortest-lived basis and is recorded so the reason can be seen.
STOP-GAPS (each with its trigger, and a comment STOP-GAP(P2-12 slice N) that a test greps so none is forgotten): the phone keeps name-based ownership marking (LibraryMatcher.findArtist) for search rows with no libraryArtistId; cost: the phone still owns a matcher (B-46 partly open); trigger: slice 8's errand has identified every library artist. alerts_service.dart keeps its own map until slice 6; trigger: slice 6 deletes alerts.catalogueArtistIds; P2-15 then removes the phone's release check. NEVER a phone-side column: the N-14 note's interim "persist the matched id per library artist on the phone" is rejected; it would be a fifth place to repair and slice 3 deletes it.
